frs_sections.title: OVERVIEW
frs_sections.content:
=====================================================================

DDR5 SDRAM (Double Data Rate 5 Synchronous Dynamic Random Access
Memory) is the fifth-generation mainstream double-data-rate DRAM
defined by the JEDEC Standard JESD79-5. DDR5 is the successor to
DDR4 (JESD79-4) and targets higher bandwidth, higher capacity, and
improved channel efficiency at lower operating voltage. DDR5 raises
the per-pin data rate from the DDR4 ceiling of 3200 MT/s up to
DDR5-8400 and beyond, while reducing VDD/VDDQ from 1.2 V (DDR4) to
1.1 V (DDR5).

The single most defining architectural change in DDR5 relative to
DDR4 is the split of each DIMM channel into TWO INDEPENDENT
SUB-CHANNELS. A DDR4 DIMM presents a single 64-bit data bus (72-bit
with ECC). A DDR5 DIMM instead presents two independent 32-b…

frs_sections.title: TWO INDEPENDENT SUB-CHANNEL ARCHITECTURE
frs_sections.content:
=====================================================================

A DDR5 UDIMM/RDIMM is partitioned into two independent sub-channels,
commonly labeled Sub-Channel A and Sub-Channel B.

  - Each sub-channel is 32 data bits wide (DQ[31:0]) plus, when ECC is
    present, 8 additional bits, giving 40 bits per sub-channel.
  - Each sub-channel has its OWN command/address (CA) bus, its OWN
    chip-select(s) (CS_n), and its OWN clock (CK_t/CK_c).
  - The two sub-channels are addressed and trained independently. A
    read or write on Sub-Channel A is unrelated to traffic on
    Sub-Channel B.

This contrasts with DDR4, where a DIMM presents a single 64-bit
(72-bit ECC) data path shared by one CA bus. The DDR5 two-sub-channel
split, combined with BL16, keeps each access at a 64-byte cache-l…

frs_sections.title: BANKS, BANK GROUPS, AND SAME-BANK REFRESH
frs_sections.content:
=====================================================================

DDR5 organizes its array into banks grouped into bank groups:
  - x4 / x8 device: 32 banks in 8 bank groups (4 banks per group).
  - x16 device: 16 banks in 4 bank groups (4 banks per group).

Bank groups allow back-to-back accesses to different groups to hide
the column-to-column delay (tCCD_L within a group vs tCCD_S across
groups), as in DDR4 but with twice the bank count.

Refresh:
  - DDR5 retains all-bank refresh (REFab) and adds SAME-BANK REFRESH
    (REFsb), where a refresh targets the same bank number across all
    bank groups, leaving the other banks available for access.
  - Same-bank refresh improves availability by allowing the controller
    to keep other banks open during a refresh.
  - DDR5 supports fin…

frs_sections.title: SPEED BINS AND DATA RATES
frs_sections.content:
=====================================================================

DDR5 speed bins span from DDR5-3200 up to DDR5-8400 and beyond. Each
bin names the data rate in MT/s (mega-transfers per second):

  DDR5-3200   3200 MT/s   1600 MHz clock
  DDR5-3600   3600 MT/s   1800 MHz clock
  DDR5-4000   4000 MT/s   2000 MHz clock
  DDR5-4400   4400 MT/s   2200 MHz clock
  DDR5-4800   4800 MT/s   2400 MHz clock
  DDR5-5200   5200 MT/s   2600 MHz clock
  DDR5-5600   5600 MT/s   2800 MHz clock
  DDR5-6000   6000 MT/s   3000 MHz clock
  DDR5-6400   6400 MT/s   3200 MHz clock
  DDR5-7200   7200 MT/s   3600 MHz clock
  DDR5-8000   8000 MT/s   4000 MHz clock
  DDR5-8400   8400 MT/s   4200 MHz clock

Data is double-data-rate: two beats per clock period (one per CK edge),
so DDR5-6400 has a 3200 MHz clock…

frs_sections.title: SUPPLY VOLTAGES
frs_sections.content:
=====================================================================

DDR5 lowers the core/IO supply relative to DDR4:
  - VDD  = 1.1 V (core)        (DDR4: 1.2 V)
  - VDDQ = 1.1 V (DQ IO)       (DDR4: 1.2 V)
  - VPP  = 1.8 V (wordline pump, same as DDR4)

The lower 1.1 V VDD/VDDQ reduces dynamic and IO power at iso-frequency.
On a DIMM, these rails are produced on-module by the PMIC from the
12 V host supply (see Section 11).

9. INTERNAL VREF AND TRAINING (VrefDQ / VrefCA)
=====================================================================

frs_sections.title: MODE REGISTERS
frs_sections.content:
=====================================================================

DDR5 greatly expands the Mode Register (MR) space relative to DDR4.
Where DDR4 had a handful of mode registers (MR0..MR7), DDR5 defines
many more (MR0 through MRxx, dozens of registers) covering, among
others:
  - MR0: Burst length, CAS latency (read latency).
  - MR2: write latency, 2N mode.
  - Mode registers for DFE tap coefficients.
  - Mode registers for VrefDQ / VrefCA settings.
  - Mode registers for on-die ECC control and error reporting.
  - Mode registers for refresh management (RFM), ECS scrubbing.
  - Mode registers for duty-cycle adjustment (DCA) and Tx/Rx
    equalization.
Mode Register Write (MRW) and Mode Register Read (MRR) commands access
these registers over the 2-cycle CA protocol.

frs_sections.title: DISTINCTION FROM SIBLING MEMORY STANDARDS
frs_sections.content:
=====================================================================

DDR5 (JESD79-5) is distinguished from related JEDEC memory standards:

  - vs DDR3 (JESD79-3): DDR3 is 1.5 V, uses a DLL, a single 64/72-bit
    data bus, BL8, no bank groups, no DFE, no sub-channels, and no
    on-module PMIC. DDR5 is 1.1 V, two 32-bit sub-channels, BL16, DFE,
    on-die ECC, DIMM PMIC.
  - vs DDR4 (JESD79-4): DDR4 is 1.2 V, has bank groups and a single
    64/72-bit bus, BL8, gear-down mode, NO DFE, NO sub-channels, NO
    on-die ECC standard, and NO on-module PMIC. DDR5's defining
    additions over DDR4 are the two sub-channels, DFE, on-die ECC,
    same-bank refresh, and the DIMM PMIC/SPD-hub.
  - vs LPDDR5 (JESD209-5): LPDDR5 is the low-power mobile generation
    using a separate Write Clock (WCK…

protocol_overview.type: Parallel, source-synchronous, double-data-rate synchronous DRAM (JESD79-5). Each DIMM is split into two independent 32-bit (40-bit ECC) sub-channels; commands use a 2-cycle CA protocol; data is double-pumped on DQS strobes.
protocol_overview.duplex: Half-duplex bidirectional DQ bus per sub-channel (reads and writes share DQ, captured on the bidirectional DQS_t/DQS_c strobe).
protocol_overview.channel_independence: The 16 channels are completely independent and not necessarily synchronous to each other; each has its own CK_t/CK_c and command/address bus.
protocol_overview.pseudo_channel_mode: Each 64-bit channel splits into two 32-bit pseudo-channels that share the channel's CA bus and clock but execute column commands independently.
protocol_overview.ddr_signaling: Data (DQ) sampled on both edges of the data strobe (double data rate). Commands registered at the rising edges of CK_t/CK_c. Write data framed by WDQS_t/WDQS_c; read data by RDQS_t/RDQS_c.
protocol_overview.controller_role: Host-side memory controller is bus master: drives per-channel CK_t/CK_c, row (R) and column (C) buses, write data + WDQS; sinks read data + RDQS; schedules refresh/RFM and handles link-ECC + RAS.
protocol_overview.dram_role: The DRAM stack is the target: each channel decodes row/column commands, manages banks/bank-groups, performs on-die ECC, drives read data + RDQS, sinks write data + WDQS, reports TEMP/alerts.

clock: CK_t, CK_c (per-channel differential; commands on rising edges)

protocol_overview.encoding: Unencoded parallel binary on DQ; optional Data Bus Inversion (DBI) to limit simultaneous switching; write CRC and command/address parity for integrity. Data is captured on both edges of DQS_t/DQS_c (double data rate).
protocol_overview.modulation: Single-ended POD-style DQ signaling referenced to internal VrefDQ; differential CK_t/CK_c clock and DQS_t/DQS_c strobe.
protocol_overview.topology: DIMM -> two independent sub-channels -> bank groups -> banks; RDIMM adds RCD; module carries PMIC + SPD hub.

compliance_requirements: Two independent 32-bit (40-bit ECC) sub-channels per DIMM.
Decision Feedback Equalization (DFE) on the DQ receivers.
On-die ECC (ODECC) in every device; Error Check and Scrub (ECS).
32 banks / 8 bank groups (x8); all-bank and same-bank refresh.
Internal VrefDQ / VrefCA with CA / read / write training.
2-cycle CA command protocol over CA[13:0]; expanded mode registers.
DIMM PMIC + SPD hub + RCD module architecture.

DIMM-LEVEL POWER (PMIC), SPD HUB, AND RCD

functional_requirements.text: Each DDR5 DIMM is partitioned into two INDEPENDENT 32-bit (40-bit with ECC) sub-channels, each with its own command/address bus, chip-select, and clock; the two sub-channels operate independently.

The DDR5 SDRAM applies Decision Feedback Equalization (DFE) on its DQ receivers to cancel post-cursor inter-symbol interference; DFE tap coefficients are tuned during write training and stored in mode registers.

Every DDR5 device implements On-Die ECC (ODECC), a single-error-correcting code computed and checked inside the die, transparent to the host; an Error Check and Scrub (ECS) mode scrubs accumulated errors.
The array is organized as 32 banks in 8 bank groups for x4/x8 devices (16 banks / 4 groups for x16); tCCD_L applies within a bank group and tCCD_S across bank groups.

DDR5 supports all-bank refresh (REFab) and same-bank refresh (REFsb), which refreshes the same bank number across all bank groups while leaving other banks accessible, plus fine-granularity and temperature-controlled refresh.
The native burst length is BL16 (16 beats; 64-byte access per 32-bit sub-channel), with BL32 burst-chop and on-the-fly burst-length control.
DDR5 supports speed bins from DDR5-3200 (3200 MT/s) to DDR5-8400+ MT/s; data is double-data-rate (two beats per CK period).
VDD = VDDQ = 1.1 V and VPP = 1.8 V, lower than DDR4's 1.2 V VDD/VDDQ.
VrefDQ and VrefCA are generated and trimmed inside the DDR5 device and centered during read/write/CA training (write leveling, read DQ calibration, CA training, MPC-driven modes).
Commands use a 2-cycle CA protocol over CA[13:0] with a per-sub-channel CS_n; the command set includes ACTIVATE, READ, WRITE, PRECHARGE, REFRESH (REFab/REFsb), self refresh, MRW/MRR, and MPC.

DDR5 greatly expands the mode-register space (MR0..MRxx) relative to DDR4, covering burst length, CAS latency, DFE taps, VrefDQ/VrefCA, on-die-ECC control, refresh management, and equalization, accessed via MRW/MRR.

Power management moves onto the DIMM: an on-module Power Management IC (PMIC) generates the 1.1 V / 1.8 V rails from 12 V, an SPD hub holds configuration and buffers the sideband bus, and RDIMMs add a Registering Clock Driver (RCD).

error_response_conditions: On-die ECC single-bit error — corrected inside the device before the data leaves the die; counts reportable via mode registers.
Write CRC error — flagged on ALERT_n; the controller retries the write.
Command/Address parity error — flagged on ALERT_n; the command is blocked and recovery is initiated.
Refresh/timing violation — a missed refresh or a tRCD/tRP/tRAS violation risks data loss; the controller must honor the timing parameters.
